title: Noughts & Crosses · Part 1 — Sequence before loops
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: sequence — Instructions that run in a specified order.
statement — One instruction in a program.
output — Information shown by the program.
2D array — Values stored using two indexes.
row — A horizontal line of values.
column — A vertical line of values.

blocks.title: Start with sequence
blocks.text: Write the five lines in the left panel into a C# console program. Run it. There are no loops ; each statement executes in order.

blocks.title: Make one simple change
blocks.text: Change the middle square 5 to X. Which exact line do you edit? This works — but changing the text every time a player moves is awkward.

blocks.title: Store the squares as data
blocks.text: Put the nine square values into a 2D array. The first index chooses the row; the second chooses the column. Try board[1,1] = "X"; : the data changes without rewriting every display instruction.

blocks.title: Display the data directly
blocks.text: Write the first row explicitly using three array accesses. Then do the same for rows 1 and 2. Notice: almost the same code is needed for every row. We will use that repetition to discover loops in Lesson 014.

blocks.title: Worked example · Make the board display before improving it
blocks.text: Start with separate instructions; then make the output read from array values. 1 | 2 | 3 --+---+-- 4 | 5 | 6 --+---+-- 7 | 8 | 9
